contents.name: Lemma 1: refinement Condition C yields Kolmogorov-consistent cylinder laws
contents.reason: The lemma constructs a cylinder-law extension from partition consistency; this pair proves a countably additive random probability measure by an explicit Poisson construction, so the projective route is not used as a substitute.

contents.name: Definition 1: Dirichlet-process finite-partition specification
contents.support: This is the finite-partition law convention used locally; the carrier adds the evaluation sigma-algebra, zero-base cell convention, and an explicit existence theorem.

contents.name: Proposition 1: zero-base cells and positive-cell mass
contents.support: The proposition supports the zero-base mass convention and finite-partition boundary discussion; the local existence proof derives zero increments and the positive-cell law.

contents.name: Proposition 2: sigma-additivity of a DP sample when the base is sigma-additive
contents.locator: Section 3, Proposition 2 and proof, printed pp. 215–216.
contents.support: The source identifies countable additivity as a separate issue; the local construction proves countable additivity directly through a weighted sum of Dirac measures.

contents.name: Proposition 3: support under the pointwise-convergence topology
contents.locator: Section 3, Proposition 3 and proof, printed pp. 216–217.
contents.reason: The proposition explicitly selects pointwise-convergence topology and a fixed support target; this pair makes no weak-support or contraction claim and records that such topology and prior-mass hypotheses must be specified separately.

contents.name: Definition 2: conditionally IID sample from a random probability measure
contents.support: The local posterior theorem states its conditional product-kernel model explicitly and proves a measurable posterior version on the full evaluation sigma-algebra.

contents.name: Proposition 4: prior-predictive marginal of one draw
contents.locator: Section 3, Proposition 4 and proof, printed p. 217.
contents.support: The local Pólya-urn theorem derives the general n-draw predictive ratio, including the zero and one boundary cases.

contents.name: Proposition 5: one-draw conditional partition probabilities
contents.locator: Section 3, Proposition 5 and proof, printed pp. 217–218.
contents.support: Supports the finite-partition one-observation update; the local proof establishes the data-indexed kernel and extends its disintegration identity.

contents.name: Theorem 1: finite-partition posterior remains a Dirichlet process
contents.locator: Section 3, Theorem 1 and complete proof, printed pp. 218–219.
contents.support: The source gives the finite-partition conjugate posterior; the local argument adds kernel measurability and null-fiber version handling.

contents.name: Section 4 alternative gamma-process jump representation (Theorem 1 from reference [4])
contents.locator: Section 4, opening and Theorem 1, printed p. 219.
contents.reason: This alternative route invokes an external gamma-process jump theorem; the controlling design requires a local Poisson-random-measure construction and does not assume gamma-process existence.

contents.name: Section 4 Theorem 2: normalized gamma-process jumps yield a DP
contents.locator: Section 4, Theorem 2 and proof, printed pp. 219–220.
contents.reason: The argument depends on the cited gamma-process jump representation and its external theorem; the local carrier proves the normalized-Gamma law from finite strips without importing that result.

contents.name: Section 4 Theorem 3: integrability and mean of DP integrals
contents.locator: Section 4, Theorem 3 and proof, printed p. 220.
contents.reason: This moment identity is not needed for finite-partition existence, posterior disintegration, or prediction in this pair; no broader DP integral-moment theorem is claimed.

contents.name: Section 4 Theorem 4: covariance of DP integrals
contents.locator: Section 4, Theorem 4 and proof, printed pp. 220–221.
contents.reason: The covariance formula is outside the assigned finite-partition scope and does not imply weak support, density consistency, or contraction; none of those claims is made locally.

item_arguments.argument: Defines the measurable counting-measure evaluation sigma-algebra and independent Poisson counts on every finite-intensity disjoint family, including the zero-mean point mass convention.
Defines DP(alpha), when it exists, through the evaluation sigma-algebra and finite-partition Dirichlet laws, omitting zero-base cells and stating the one-positive-cell convention.

Partitions the mark axis into finite-intensity strips, constructs independent Poisson counts and marks by standard-Borel product extension, proves the projected counting measure is Poisson, derives normalized-Gamma increments by a Laplace transform, normalizes to a random probability measure, and proves uniqueness on evaluation cylinders.

Represents a positive Dirichlet vector by normalized independent shape-rate Gamma variables, computes grouped Gamma transforms, uses transform uniqueness, and normalizes; the one-group case is checked directly.

Proves data measurability on finite evaluation cylinders, extends it to a probability kernel, refines observation and posterior partitions, applies finite Dirichlet-multinomial conjugacy on positive-evidence blocks, and extends disintegration by finite-measure uniqueness while preserving the null-fiber caveat.
Computes posterior base masses of a set and its complement, applies one-trial Dirichlet-multinomial evidence when both are positive, and handles deterministic zero/one boundary cases.
Records the scope boundary: finite-partition construction and update specify neither a topology nor a density model, so weak-support and contraction claims need separate hypotheses and proofs.
Substitutes alpha=(2,1,1) and counts (1,1,0), obtains posterior (3,2,1), checks next probabilities (1/2,1/3,1/6), and computes P(X1=a,X2=a)=3/10.
On X={a,b}, alpha=delta_a, verifies P(X1=b)=0, changes the posterior kernel at that null fiber, checks disintegration is unchanged, and records the diffuse-base singleton case.
